```{r typst-helpers}
# ---- Small helpers for writing Typst from R --------------------------------

# Escape text so Typst prints it literally (no accidental *bold*, _italic_,
# #code, @refs, $math$, or // comments).
esc <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "([\\\\#*_`$@<>\\[\\]~/])", "\\\\\\1")

# Quote a value as a Typst string literal, e.g. for URLs and file names.
typst_str <- function(x) paste0('"', str_replace_all(x, '(["\\\\])', "\\\\\\1"), '"')

# Character column cleanup: NA -> "", strip LaTeX "\&" left over from the
# old CV, collapse repeated spaces, and drop stray spaces before commas.
clean <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[is.na(x)] <- ""
  x <- str_replace_all(x, fixed("\\&"), "&")
  x <- str_squish(x)
  str_replace_all(x, "\\s+,", ",")
}

# APA 7: DOIs are shown as https://doi.org/ URLs with no trailing period
apa_doi <- function(x) {
  x <- str_replace(x, "^(doi:\\s*|https?://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/)", "https://doi.org/")
  str_remove(x, "\\.$")
}

# Add a period unless the text already ends in . ? or !
end_punct <- function(x) if_else(str_detect(x, "[.?!]$"), x, paste0(x, "."))

# OSF badges: "\img{osfdata.png}{https://osf.io/x}..." -> linked Typst icons
osf_badges <- function(s) {
  m <- str_match_all(s, "\\\\img\\{([^}]*)\\}\\{([^}]*)\\}")[[1]]
  if (nrow(m) == 0) return("")
  paste0(" ", paste0("#icon(", typst_str(m[, 2]), ", ", typst_str(m[, 3]), ")",
                     collapse = "#h(1pt)"))
}

# Emit a "label | entry" list. `labels` and `entries` are Typst markup strings.
labelled_list <- function(labels, entries, width, label_size = "10pt",
                          label_align = "right") {
  rows <- sprintf("  ([%s], [%s]),", labels, entries)
  knitr::raw_block(
    paste(c(sprintf("#labelled-list(%s, label-size: %s, label-align: %s, (",
                    width, label_size, label_align),
            rows, "))"),
          collapse = "\n"),
    type = "typst"
  )
}
```

```{r grants}
# ---- External funding -------------------------------------------------------
# Edit the wording/order of each grant entry here.
funds <- read_excel(xl, sheet = "Grants")

grants_list <- function(d, cond) {
  d <- d |>
    filter(status == cond) |>
    arrange(desc(end)) |>
    mutate(
      authors = esc(str_remove(clean(authors), "\\.$")),
      title   = esc(clean(title)),
      funder  = esc(clean(funder)),
      number  = if_else(clean(number) == "", "", paste0(" ", esc(clean(number)), ".")),
      dates   = paste0(format(start, "%B %Y"), " -- ", format(end, "%B %Y")),
      amount  = paste0("#money[\\", scales::dollar(amount), "]"),
      entry   = paste0(authors, ". (", year, "). _", title, "_. ", funder, ".",
                       number, " ", dates, ". ", amount, ".")
    )
  labelled_list(esc(clean(d$type)), d$entry, width = "1.9cm",
                label_size = "9pt", label_align = "left")
}
```

```{r journals}
# ---- Peer-reviewed journal articles ----------------------------------------
# Edit the citation format here. Your name is bolded by the Typst template.
pubs <- read_excel(xl, sheet = "Journals", col_types = "text") |>
  mutate(across(everything(), clean))

pubs_list <- function(d) {
  d <- d |>
    mutate(
      # year label only on the first article of each year
      label  = if_else(year != lag(year, default = ""), year, ""),
      source = paste0("_", esc(journal), "_"),
      source = if_else(volume != "", paste0(source, ", _", esc(volume), "_"), source),
      source = if_else(issue  != "", paste0(source, "(", esc(issue), ")"), source),
      source = if_else(pages  != "", paste0(source, ", ", esc(pages)), source),
      doi    = apa_doi(doi),
      doi    = if_else(doi != "", paste0(" #link(", typst_str(doi), ")"), ""),
      badges = vapply(opensci, osf_badges, character(1)),
      entry  = paste0(esc(authors), " (", tolower(year), "). ",
                      esc(end_punct(title)), " ", source, ".", doi, badges)
    )
  labelled_list(d$label, d$entry, width = "1.65cm")
}
```

```{r scholar}
# ---- Google Scholar ---------------------------------------------------------
# Refresh when possible; otherwise fall back to the last good pull.
scholar_cache <- "_scholar-cache.json"
scholar_info <- tryCatch({
  if (!isTRUE(params$fetch_scholar)) stop("offline render")
  library(scholar)
  httr::set_config(httr::user_agent("Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; R scholar package)"))
  id <- "UWdXXEoAAAAJ"
  prof <- get_profile(id)
  out <- list(
    citations = prof$total_cites,
    h_index   = prof$h_index,
    fetched   = as.character(Sys.Date()),
    history   = get_citation_history(id)
  )
  write_json(out, scholar_cache, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
  out
}, error = function(e) read_json(scholar_cache, simplifyVector = TRUE))

# Installed package version and release year, with last-known values as a
# fallback (used in the Software section)
pkg_info <- function(pkg) {
  last_known <- list(
    data.table        = c("1.18.6.1", "2026"),
    furniture         = c("1.11.0", "2026"),
    tidyfast          = c("0.4.0", "2024"),
    MarginalMediation = c("0.7.3", "2026"),
    autoscore         = c("0.5.0", "2019"),
    dissertateUSU     = c("0.3.1", "2019"),
    rjasa             = c("0.1.1", "2019")
  )
  known <- last_known[[pkg]]
  tryCatch({
    d <- packageDescription(pkg)
    if (!is.list(d)) stop("not installed")
    # an older installed copy shouldn't roll the CV back
    if (package_version(d$Version) <= package_version(known[1])) stop("older")
    date <- c(d[["Date/Publication"]], d[["Date"]], d[["Packaged"]])[1]
    c(d$Version, substr(date, 1, 4))
  }, error = function(e) known)
}
pkg_version <- function(pkg) pkg_info(pkg)[1]
pkg_year    <- function(pkg) pkg_info(pkg)[2]
```

```{r citation-history, eval = params$cite_fig, results = "asis", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 2.3, out.width = "100%"}
cat("\n# CITATION COUNT HISTORY\n\n")

library(ggplot2)
citations <- as.data.frame(scholar_info$history)
month <- months(Sys.Date())
year  <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")

ggplot(citations, aes(year, cites, fill = year)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = cites),
            nudge_y = 40) +
  labs(x = "Year",
       y = "Citation Count\n(by Year)",
       caption = paste("Note: Data for citations in", year, "until", month)) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1,
                       begin = .1,
                       end = .9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024, 2026, 2028)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = .4))
ggsave("citation_count.png", width = 7, height = 4)
```
